Overview

Luxembourg as a Business Centre

Luxembourg City is a small capital with an outsized financial role. It had 137,696 residents at the end of 2025, drawn from 168 nationalities, with Luxembourgers accounting for around 30 percent of the population. Yet the country it anchors is Europe's largest investment fund centre: the CSSF reported fund net assets of about EUR 6.4 trillion across 2,850 undertakings for collective investment in February 2026, alongside 117 banks and more than 61,000 people employed in the financial sector. The city is also one of the European Union's three institutional seats, with around 14,000 people working for European institutions, and sits at the centre of a Greater Region spanning parts of France, Belgium and Germany.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Luxembourg City because so many international structures pass through it. A private equity platform, a family holding or a property portfolio may be owned through one or more Luxembourg companies whose managers are professional service providers rather than the people who control the money. Lenders and claimants need to know what sits behind a Luxembourg holding before they lend, sue or enforce. Fund sponsors, depositaries and investors need background research on managers and counterparties. Litigants before the district court in Luxembourg City or in arbitration seated there need well-sourced facts about parties whose operating business is often elsewhere.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Luxembourg

01

Holding company look-through research

Establishing who stands behind a Luxembourg City holding or financing company whose directors are corporate service providers, by combining register filings and published accounts with foreign registries, litigation records and media, so lenders and counterparties understand the operating group and the people who actually make decisions.

02

Fund manager and sponsor background

Background research on alternative investment fund managers, sponsors and key individuals before an allocation, a co-investment or a service mandate, covering regulatory history, prior funds, disputes, business associations and reputation across the jurisdictions where the principals have worked.

03

Asset tracing through layered structures

Supporting counsel seeking to enforce judgments or awards where assets are held through Luxembourg companies, by mapping intra-group shareholdings, financing flows visible in filed accounts and connected entities abroad, to help identify where protective measures before the Luxembourg courts may be worth considering.

04

Real estate holding structures

Research into the companies that hold European commercial property portfolios through Luxembourg vehicles, including changes of ownership, related-party lending and the individuals behind successive acquisitions, for buyers, financiers and parties to valuation or partnership disputes.

05

Cross-border workforce misconduct

Fact-finding support for counsel at Luxembourg City entities whose staff commute from France, Belgium and Germany, where suspected conflicts of interest, expense fraud or diversion of business require background research on vendors and associates across several national record systems.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Luxembourg

District court of Luxembourg

Commercial claims over EUR 15,000 or of undetermined value go to the Tribunal d'arrondissement. In Luxembourg City the court has 15 chambers, three of which, the 2nd, 6th and 15th, specialise in commercial matters. Its President, sitting as summary judge, can order urgent and protective measures, and ex parte orders are available where surprise is needed, which is why clear facts about a counterparty's Luxembourg assets matter early.

Appeal courts in the capital

Appeals from the district court go to the Court of Appeal, and the Cour de cassation sits at the top of the ordinary courts, ruling only on points of law. Smaller claims under EUR 15,000 go to the justice of the peace. Judges can accept evidence in French, German, Luxembourgish and English without translation, which can simplify the use of English-language research reports in proceedings.

Chamber of Commerce arbitration

The Arbitration Centre of the Chamber of Commerce of Luxembourg is governed by a five-member council that includes the chair of ICC Luxembourg, the President of the Bar and the Chamber's Director General. The default place of arbitration is the Chamber itself, there is no compulsory list of arbitrators and the language of proceedings is open. Investigative support is limited to factual research for counsel and the parties.

CSSF and the fund ecosystem

The CSSF, based in Luxembourg City, supervises banks, investment funds, fund managers and other financial professionals. Its published lists of authorised entities and statistics help confirm whether a fund, manager or service provider is supervised. Supervision is not a guarantee of the integrity of individuals, so manager diligence still requires independent research into people and track records. Diligence on a Luxembourg City manager therefore checks the regulatory position first and then the people.

European institutions

Luxembourg is one of the three seats of the European Union institutions, alongside Brussels and Strasbourg, and around 14,000 people work for European bodies in the country. Matters involving EU-funded projects, EU-level litigation or individuals moving between institutions and the private financial sector can therefore have a Luxembourg City dimension. Research in such matters stays with public records, published decisions and open sources, and does not extend to internal institutional information.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Luxembourg

For matters touching Luxembourg City, TDSC starts by locating the Luxembourg entity within the wider structure and deciding which questions the capital's records can actually answer. Research is conducted from Nashville using register filings, published accounts, CSSF lists, court reporting and French, German and English-language sources, then extended into the jurisdictions where owners and operating businesses sit. Where interviews, document retrieval or other local steps are justified, TDSC coordinates with qualified local professionals and the client's Luxembourg counsel rather than acting directly. Findings are reported with their sources so counsel can decide what may support summary or protective applications before the Luxembourg courts.

TDSC has no office in Luxembourg. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Luxembourg: Frequently Asked Questions

Why do so many investigations lead to a Luxembourg City company?

Because the capital hosts a large share of Europe's fund, holding and financing vehicles. Private equity, real estate and family wealth are often held through Luxembourg companies managed by professional directors. The Luxembourg entity is rarely where decisions are made, so useful research usually starts in Luxembourg and then follows the structure to the owners and operating businesses in other countries.

Which court in Luxembourg City would hear our commercial claim?

Claims over EUR 15,000 or of undetermined value go to the district court, where three chambers in Luxembourg City specialise in commercial matters. Smaller claims go to the justice of the peace. Appeals go to the Court of Appeal and points of law to the Cour de cassation. Your Luxembourg counsel will confirm the forum; we support them with factual research.

Can you confirm that a Luxembourg fund manager is regulated?

We can check the CSSF's published lists and statistics to see whether an entity appears as authorised, and research its history, principals and disputes. Authorisation shows supervision, not the conduct of the individuals involved, so we combine regulatory checks with background research on the people running the business in Luxembourg City and elsewhere.

Is arbitration in Luxembourg City common for commercial disputes?

The Chamber of Commerce runs an arbitration centre with its own rules, a governing council drawn from the business and legal community and flexible language arrangements. Many international parties also seat ICC or other institutional arbitrations in Luxembourg. In either case TDSC's role is limited to factual research for counsel and the parties.

Does TDSC have an office in Luxembourg City?

No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Luxembourg. Most Luxembourg work is desk-based research using public and commercial sources. Where local steps are needed, we coordinate with qualified local professionals and the client's Luxembourg counsel, and we do not seek bank, fund or account information that is not lawfully available.
